claims.claim: Hobb says something about the Robin Hobb style does not lend itself to tales shorter than a novella.
claims.quote: Something about the style does not lend itself to shorter tales

claims.claim: Dray characterises all of Hobb's works as marked by a general glum realism.
claims.source: Stephanie Dray, Strange Horizons review of the Liveship Traders series, 2001
claims.quote: the general glum realism of all of her works
claims.page: body, paragraph on Ship of Destiny

claims.claim: Justin Landon says Fool's Assassin is, without question, a slow novel.
claims.source: Justin Landon, Tor.com review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: It is, without question, a slow novel

claims.claim: Oliver identifies extensive parataxis, elevated figurative language and parallelism as the elevated fantasy style Fitz shifts into when he narrates an invented vision.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.page: pp. 59-60, section on the duchess's vision

claims.claim: The 1997 Encyclopedia of Fantasy entry on Megan Lindholm calls her a restless and varied fantasist possessing real talents.
claims.source: Encyclopedia of Fantasy (1997), 'Lindholm, Megan', entry signed DP, eds John Clute and John Grant
claims.quote: A restless and varied fantasist, Lindholm possesses real talents

claims.claim: Langford ends his praise of Assassin's Quest by saying there are a few too many pages.
claims.source: Dave Langford, SFX #24 review of Assassin's Quest, April 1997 (Ansible archive)
claims.quote: although there are a few too many pages
claims.page: the Assassin's Quest entry, final paragraph

claims.claim: Alison Flood says Hobb gives the reader months and years of not much happening before events spiral.
claims.source: Alison Flood, The Guardian review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: Hobb gives us months – years – of not much happening

claims.claim: Locus Magazine's own Index to Interviews lists only two Robin Hobb interviews, dated January 1998 and December 2005.
claims.page: index row for Hobb, linking Jan 1998 and Dec 2005

claims.claim: Hodunok finds that in the Farseer trilogy the importance of the struggle for power to the characters is significantly reduced.
claims.source: Zoriana Hodunok, Visnyk LNU imeni Tarasa Shevchenka, Filolohichni nauky 2(361), 2024, pp. 148-156
claims.quote: the importance of the power struggle for the characters is significantly reduced

claims.feature: other: coverage - Hobb absent from the epic-fantasy style monograph
claims.claim: Grimbeek's chapter-by-chapter review of Oliver's Magic Words, Magic Worlds names Erikson, Donaldson, Martin, Kuang, Le Guin, Bakker, Cook, Jemisin, Sanderson, Moorcock, Gemmell, Leiber and Jordan as its examples and never names Robin Hobb.
claims.source: Marinette Grimbeek, review of Matthew Oliver's Magic Words, Magic Worlds, Fantasy/Animation, 2 December 2022

claims.claim: The essayist reads Hobb's choice to open the book with an attempt at a history rather than with the narrator's abandonment as itself characterising the narrator.
claims.source: riddbook (video essayist), 'Robin Hobb is a literary genius. Here's why.', YouTube
claims.quote: begin the book with an attempt at a history

claims.feature: other: register compared to literary domestic fiction
claims.claim: The essayist claims Hobb bridges epic fantasy world-building with the sentence-level work and narrative scope of literary craft.
claims.source: riddbook (video essayist), 'Robin Hobb is a literary genius. Here's why.', YouTube
claims.quote: beautiful sentence level work and narrative scope of literary craft

claims.claim: Hobb says she enjoys rewriting more than first drafts, and describes the rewrite partly as removing the paragraphs that did not work.
claims.source: Robin Hobb interviewed by blinkbox Books, 'Robin Hobb explains how writing is like chasing butterflies', YouTube
claims.quote: it's taking off the paragraphs that didn't work

claims.claim: A reader disputes the common description of Hobb's characters as morally grey, saying she knows exactly who the good guys and the bad guys are.
claims.source: Allison Annotated, 'Robin Hobb Doesn't Write "Morally Grey" Characters (And Other Farseer Musings)', YouTube
claims.quote: I know exactly who the good guys and the bad
